walkthroughs.body_html:
The medieval period in Britain ran from 1066 (the Norman Conquest) to 1485 (the end of the Wars of the Roses).

It was a world without electricity, phones or printed books. Most people were farmers who never travelled more than a few miles from their village.

The king was at the top, and almost everyone else served someone above them. 👑

The feudal system was like a pyramid. The king owned all the land.

He gave land to lords (barons) in return for soldiers and loyalty. Lords gave smaller bits of land to knights, who promised to fight for them.

At the bottom, peasants worked the land. They farmed for their lord and were given protection in return.

The Normans built motte-and-bailey castles — a wooden tower on a mound (motte) with a courtyard (bailey) below. Later, stone castles replaced them.

A knight trained from age 7 as a page, then a squire, before being knighted at about 21. He wore chain mail and fought on horseback with a sword and lance. ⚔️

options: The Pope
The king
The knights

mcqs.q: How did the feudal system work in Norman England?
options: Feudalism meant peasants were slaves owned by the king.
Feudalism was a written constitution introduced by William in 1066.
The king granted land to tenants-in-chief in return for knight service; they in turn enfeoffed knights who held land in return for military service to their lord.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.

mcqs.q: Why did public health reforms accelerate after 1848?
options: Feudalism was a written constitution introduced by William in 1066.
The 1848 Public Health Act followed cholera epidemics and Chadwick's report; John Snow's 1854 Broad Street pump study reinforced the case for clean water by 1875.
The 1875 Act made the NHS free for all workers.
Public health acts were passed because Victorians discovered germs in the 1840s.

mcqs.q: Why did William of Normandy claim the English throne in 1066?
options: Feudalism was a written constitution introduced by William in 1066.
He claimed Edward the Confessor had promised him the throne in 1051 and that Harold Godwinson had sworn an oath to support that claim in 1064.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
William invaded because he was the strongest king in Europe and wanted more land.
